content.title: About
content.content: Dried figs are the dehydrated fruits of the common fig tree (Ficus carica) that are not subjected to cooking. They have a sweet‑caramel flavor, a chewy texture, and retain most of the nutrients of fresh figs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Figs are among the oldest cultivated fruits, grown in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia.
Dried figs are a staple in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines, often used in tagines and sweet pastes.
Their natural sugar content makes them sweet without added sugar.
High in dietary fiber, dried figs are popular in health‑focused snacks.
In ancient Rome, figs symbolized fertility and abundance.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain healthy blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Dried figs provide potassium, magnesium, calcium, and iron, essential for muscle function, bone health, and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Figs contain polyphenols and vitamin K, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Heart‑healthy benefits
items.content: Potassium and fiber contribute to normal blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Bone support
items.content: Calcium and magnesium in figs help maintain bone density.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Because dried figs are sugar‑dense, people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Fig allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to severe symptoms.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: Excessive consumption of dried fruit can cause gas and gastrointestinal discomfort.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Figs contain oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried figs can be enjoyed as a snack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, baked goods, salads, or processed into pastes and sauces. Soaking them in water for 10‑15 minutes softens the texture before use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried figs in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to preserve flavor and texture. Discard any figs that show mold, off‑odors, or discoloration.
